decisions.reason: Having remained in the portfolio for several years as a core drainage component that fits the firm's modular system logic, it likely meets at least acceptable aspiration levels and is worth retaining.

As a floor-level shower drainage line aligned with the firm's strategic direction toward integrated low-profile bathroom solutions, it would normally be kept unless results had clearly fallen below aspirations.
Because this designer shower drainage line was positioned as a flagship closely tied to the firm's future direction, management would give it strong support and a long evaluation horizon and keep it.

This backflow-protected basement floor drain serves a credible specialist need within the drainage portfolio, so if it is still on the market by 2022 it likely performs near aspiration and should be retained.

Although more peripheral and likely subject to closer scrutiny than the shower and core drain lines, it still complements the firm's drainage offering and would usually be kept absent clearer signs of underperformance.
